doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Raises through Gladys Hampton and salary compared with a day job
summary: Raises mostly went through the stern but fair Gladys Hampton; he did not fare badly compared with day-job pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: If you had wanted a raise in the Hampton band, did you have to go through Gladys?
Were you ever successful in getting a raise?

Yeah. She was, one thing about her, she was a really stern businesswoman but you know, if she saw that you knew your job and what you were doing was good for the band, she wouldn’t stand in the way. She wouldn’t stand in the way. And she’d tell Hamp, she’d © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
say, you know, “let me offer these musicians — let them exhibit their talents as they can” you know.
Did you ever stop while you were doing that with Hampton, stop and think about what kind of salary would I be making in a day job as opposed to what I’m doing now?
I would imagine in some industries I would making probably maybe about $50 to $100, maybe $200 more, possibly. But I wasn’t doing too bad, I wasn’t doing too bad.
